Where client work becomes repeatable

FlyRank client journeys, delivery work and automation opportunities. Source-linked evidence across the frozen 80-project portfolio.

Working review, not final sign-off. Mapped conversations are reviewed. Commercial-state comparisons, selected material sources, economic validation and final quality checks remain in progress. Nothing in this report authorizes or performs production changes.

Portfolio at a glance

The client journey

Automated generation and integrations coexist with manual setup, review, exceptions and client decisions. Episode labels describe observed service work; they are not a platform automation coverage percentage.

Observed work across accounts

Counts show accounts with reviewed work in each category. They are not failure rates, eligible automation denominators or time spent. Categories overlap.

What to build first

A small delivery ledger supports the first candidate value pilots: verified publishing, approved client facts and reconciled reporting. Improve existing features before expanding autonomy.

  1. Record obligations, ownership, approvals and verified outcomes.
  2. Prevent and detect repeated publishing and knowledge failures.
  3. Generate reports that agree with delivery records and attribution definitions.
  4. Scale only after measuring net effort and quality.

Economic discipline

No portfolio savings figure is established. The available labor sample contains self-reports, not a representative time study. Capacity released is different from cash savings.

Churn discipline

Inactive is not necessarily churned. Paused services, scope reductions, prospects and recovery work require separate states. Direct client reasons and staff hypotheses remain distinct in the dossiers.

Work inventory

Participants include client reviewers and agency contributors. A mention or assignment is not proof of who performed every step. Hours are unknown unless separately documented.

All 80 project dossiers

Database state is shown separately from the evidence-based journey. Shared-account work is not multiplied for portfolio counts.

Implementation specifications

Proposed dependency order, not a proven ROI ranking. Pilot targets are proposed acceptance gates. No production implementation has occurred.

Break-even explorer

Illustrative inputs only. Replace these with measured eligible event volume, reviewed net time savings and approved costs. No churn-recovery revenue is assumed.

Validated labor sample

Selected June 30–July 2 standups: 25 self-reported person-hours with relevant scope; 7 additional hours have unverified scope and are excluded. Plans are excluded. A two-hour bundle across three clients remains two hours, not six.

Coverage and interpretation

  • 80 project IDs match the frozen portfolio; 117 mapped packets and supplemental evidence reviewed into dossiers.
  • 527 reconstructed episodes are not exhaustive event counts. Long-running episodes may contain multiple occurrences.
  • 70 provisional account groups consolidate known shared relationships; commercial eligibility and uncertain/test/prospect strata remain under review.
  • Source references resolve locally. Linked attachments were not all read; material gaps remain stated.
  • Slack author, assigned owner and observed performer differ; actor roles must be read with the source.
  • Database configuration and source-code presence do not prove deployment, freshness or successful client execution.
  • Missing data is unknown, not zero. No statistical-significance or causal churn claim is established.
  • Observed reach, eligible opportunities, independent incidents and measured labor are separate units.
  • All original sources are preserved. This file contains synthesized findings and source links, not credentials or raw exports.
